key_points.text: Identify the inputs and outputs for a scenario, from a description, diagram or code. Outputs can be digital or hard copy.

Preconditions are what must already be true, or must be known, before a solution can work: for example, that a list is sorted, that an input is within a range, or what format data will arrive in. Stating them makes subroutines easier to reuse and test, and shows what checks the solution needs.

Caching keeps recently or frequently used data where it is faster to reach (such as web pages stored by a browser or proxy). Benefits: faster access and less load on the network or server. Drawbacks: cached data can go out of date, the cache uses storage, and deciding what to keep is complex.

Reusable program components (subroutines, classes, libraries) save development time, are already tested so have fewer errors, and keep programs consistent. For a scenario, identify the subroutines needed and which could be reused.

dont_confuse.text: Caching vs cache: caching is the technique (in software or hardware); the cache in 1.1.1 is a specific piece of fast memory in the processor.
Precondition vs input: an input is the data a solution receives; a precondition is a requirement that must hold before it runs (often about the input).
